question.text: AIF reporting should disclose financial, risk, portfolio, legal, liability, breach, PPM-change, and investee-company developments because:

answer.text: Transparent disclosure supports investor relationships and is a statutory obligation under the AIF reporting framework

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook requires periodic disclosure of financial, risk, operational, and portfolio information; material risk and liability disclosure; disclosure of breaches and legal actions; PPM-change disclosure; and investee-company developments. It also notes a statutory obligation to disclose information to maintain investor relationships. The Trap: Hiding negative developments breaches the disclosure framework and undermines investor trust. Note: Based on workbook pages 210-215 covering investor reporting and disclosure obligations.
